extraction.name: POPE
extraction.description: A polling-based query method for evaluating object hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models by formulating the evaluation as a binary classification task.
extraction.creator: Yifan Li, Yifan Du, Kun Zhou, Jinpeng Wang, Wayne Xin Zhao and Ji-Rong Wen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The evaluation dataset is constructed by selecting images from existing datasets and generating Yes/No questions based on ground-truth and nonexistent objects.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images and annotations were sourced from MSCOCO, A-OKVQA, and GQA datasets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions are built using ground-truth objects for 'Yes' answers and sampled negative objects for 'No' answers.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Object hallucination in LVLMs can lead to unexpected consequences and safety issues in real-world deployments like autonomous driving.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The visual instruction datasets share an unbalanced object distribution where top frequent objects occupy a major part of the dataset, causing models to hallucinate frequently appearing objects.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The evaluation only focuses on object hallucination and does not measure overall model capacity; it also relies on a subset of validation sets due to computational limits.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating object hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models.

name.evidence: we further design a polling-based query method called POPE for better evaluation of object hallucination.

description.evidence: The basic idea is to convert the evaluation of hallucination into a binary classification task by prompting LVLMs with simple Yes-or-Noshort questions about the probing objects

creator.evidence: Yifan Li1,3∗, Yifan Du1,3∗, Kun Zhou2∗, Jinpeng Wang4, Wayne Xin Zhao2,3†and Ji-Rong Wen1, 2,3

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We randomly select 500 images with more than 3 ground-truth objects in the annotations and construct 6 questions for each image ( i.e.,l= 6).

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: we adopt SEEM (Zou et al., 2023) to annotate images from three datasets ( i.e., MSCOCO, A-OKVQA (Schwenk et al., 2022) and GQA (Hudson and Manning, 2019)) and build POPE based on the segmentation results.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: we adopt SEEM (Zou et al., 2023) to annotate images from three datasets ( i.e., MSCOCO, A-OKVQA (Schwenk et al., 2022) and GQA (Hudson and Manning, 2019))

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Questions whose answers are “Yes” can be directly built using ground-truth objects, while questions with the answer “No” can be built by sampling from negative objects.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: We randomly select 500 images with more than 3 ground-truth objects in the annotations and construct 6 questions for each image ( i.e.,l= 6).

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: we adopt SEEM (Zou et al., 2023) to annotate images from three datasets

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: For example, due to an incorrect understanding of the extemal environment, an autonomous driving system would make wrong decisions when encountering unexpected events, which might lead to serious safety issues.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: As the visual instruction datasets of these LVLMs are mostly constructed based on MSCOCO (Lin et al., 2014), they generally share a similar unbalanced object distribution where top frequent objects occupy a major part of the dataset.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: First, we only focus on the object hallucination problem in LVLMs, while do not consider other aspects that can reflect the capacities of LVLMs... Second, due to the limitation of computation resources, we have to evaluate all models on a part of the validation set for each dataset.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: we further design a polling-based query method called POPE for better evaluation of object hallucination.
